sections.title: Intuitive Hook: From Discrete to Continuous
lecture_lines: Histograms show discrete data grouped in intervals.
Narrowing intervals smooths the chart significantly.
As data points grow, bars form a curve.
This curve is the Probability Density Function.
It describes probability density for continuous variables.
animations: Create a discrete bar chart representing individual outcomes. Color: #FFFFFF.
Morph the bars into a smooth density curve. Color: #FF7F50.
Fill the area under the curve in a light shade. Color: #87CEFA.
Highlight the peak of the density curve. Color: #FFFF00.
Label the y-axis as 'Probability Density'. Color: #FFD700.

sections.title: Defining the Core Mathematical Properties
lecture_lines: PDFs have two main mathematical properties.
First, the function must be non-negative.
Second, the total area must equal one.
Total area under the curve is always one.
animations: Display the probability mass function formula. Color: #FFFFFF.
Highlight the integral representation of probability. Color: #FF7F50.
Show the constraint that total area equals one. Color: #32CD32.
Display f(x) >= 0 constraint on screen. Color: #FF4500.
Animate total area calculation equal to 1.0. Color: #00FFFF.

sections.title: Interpreting Probability as Area
lecture_lines: Continuous variables have zero point probability.
We measure probability over an interval instead.
Area under the curve equals the probability.
Integral calculates this area between two points.
Visualize probability as a shaded curve slice.
animations: Draw a coordinate plane with a bell curve. Color: #FFFFFF.
Highlight a specific interval under the curve. Color: #FF7F50.
Shade the interval to represent probability. Color: #87CEFA.
Write the integral notation for the shaded area. Color: #FFD700.
Show point probability is zero at any x. Color: #FF0000.

sections.title: Summary and Conceptual Check
lecture_lines: PDF defines probability density, not probability itself.
The peak indicates the most likely value.
Changing parameters alters the distribution shape.
animations: Recap discrete versus continuous concepts. Color: #FFFFFF.
Show the transition process visually once more. Color: #FF7F50.
Finalize with the area-probability equivalence. Color: #32CD32.
